newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Group says Ethiopian police killed innocent man.
newsitem.headline: Group says Ethiopian police killed innocent man.

text.p: An Ethiopian human rights group said on Friday a man killed by police and accused of being the leader of an underground group was innocent and a member of its own executive committee.

The independent Ethiopian Human Rights Council said Assefa Maru, also an executive member of the Ethiopian Teachers' Association, was shot dead by police in the Capital Addis Ababa as he walked home from his office last week.
It urged the government to prevent police shooting suspects in broad daylight.
Police said Assefa was the leader of the Ethiopian United Patriotic Front and had resisted arrest and attempted to flee.
The council said Assefa was not armed when he was killed. Police said they found assault rifles and arrested other members of the underground group when they shot Assefa.
The council said his killing was a gross violation of human rights and urged the government to investigate the incident.
Police said last June the Ethiopian United Patriotic Front had planned to asssassinate government officials and foreigners.
Last month one person was killed and 86 injured in grenade attacks on a supermarket, a restaurant and two hotels frequented by foreigners in Addis Ababa and the eastern town of Dire Dawa.
